subject: maths
source: NCERT Ganita Prakash | Grade 6, Chapter 2 + BHPS midterm model paper (2026-27)

topics.name: Point, line segment, line and ray

questions.q: The shortest path between two points is a…
questions.e: A line segment is the shortest distance between two points. (Model paper Q3.)

questions.q: A line segment has…
questions.e: A line segment starts and stops at its two end points.

questions.q: A ray has…
questions.a: one starting point and goes on forever in one direction
questions.e: Ray DP starts at D and goes on through P indefinitely.

questions.q: A line…
w: can be measured with a ruler
questions.e: A line has no end points.

questions.q: A point is usually named using…
questions.e: Points are named P, Q, A …

questions.q: How many lines can pass through one given point?
questions.e: Lines in every direction can pass through a single point.

questions.q: How many lines can pass through two given points?
questions.e: Only one straight line passes through two points.

questions.q: In ray DP, which point is the starting point?
questions.e: A ray is named with its starting point first.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): We cannot measure the length of a ray.
Reason (R): A ray goes on indefinitely in one direction.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
w: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.e: A ray has no second end, so it has no fixed length. R explains A.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A line segment has a definite length.
Reason (R): A line segment extends in both directions without end.
questions.a: A is true, but R is false.
w: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.e: A is true. R describes a line, not a line segment, so R is false.

questions.q: Two rays starting from a common point form a(n)…
questions.e: An angle is formed by two rays with a common starting point. (Model paper Q5.)

questions.q: In ∠POM, the vertex is…
questions.e: The middle letter names the vertex.

questions.q: Which is another name for ∠PQR?
questions.e: The vertex Q stays in the middle.

questions.q: The rays that form an angle are called its…
questions.e: The two rays are the arms; the common point is the vertex.

questions.q: The size of an angle is…
questions.a: the amount of rotation about the vertex to turn one arm onto the other
w: the distance between the arm ends
questions.e: Size = amount of turn, not arm length.

questions.q: If the arms of an angle are made longer, the angle…
questions.e: Angle size depends on the turn, not on arm length.

questions.q: One full turn is…
questions.e: A full turn is 360°. (Model paper Q17.)

questions.q: A straight angle measures…
questions.e: Half of a full turn = 180°.

questions.q: A right angle measures…
questions.e: A quarter turn = 90°.

questions.q: An angle of 200° is…
questions.e: Reflex angles are more than 180° and less than 360°. (Model paper Q2.)

questions.q: An angle more than 90° but less than 180° is…
questions.e: Obtuse: between a right angle and a straight angle.

questions.q: Lines that meet at right angles are called…
questions.e: Perpendicular lines meet at 90°.

questions.q: How many right angles make a full turn?
Which angle is formed by the hands of a clock at 6 o'clock?
questions.e: The hands point in opposite directions: 180°.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): An angle of 90° is an acute angle.
Reason (R): Acute angles are less than 90°.
questions.a: A is false, but R is true.
w: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
questions.e: A is false: 90° is a right angle. R is true.

questions.q: The instrument used to measure angles is a…
questions.e: A protractor measures angles in degrees. (Model paper Q14.)

questions.q: When measuring an angle, the centre of the protractor is placed on the…
questions.e: Place the centre on the vertex and the base line along one arm.

questions.q: Why does a protractor have two scales (inner and outer)?
questions.a: So an angle can be measured from either side (left or right arm)
w: One is in cm and one in inches
One is for acute and one for obtuse angles
questions.e: Use the scale that starts at 0° on the arm lying along the base line.

questions.q: To draw an angle of 80° at point O on ray OA, which step comes first after placing the protractor?
questions.a: Put the centre on O and the base line along OA, then mark 80° from the 0° side
w: Draw any line and measure it with a ruler
questions.e: Always count from the 0° that sits on the given arm. (Model paper Q38a.)

questions.q: {n} points are marked so that no three lie on one line. How many line segments join them in pairs?
questions.e: Each point joins {nm} others; each segment is counted twice: {n} × {nm} ÷ 2 = {ans}.

questions.q: Points A, B and C lie on a line in that order. How many different line segments can be named using them?
questions.e: AB, BC and AC.

questions.q: Ray AB and ray BA are…
questions.a: different rays – they start at different points and go in opposite directions
questions.e: A ray is named from its starting point; AB starts at A, BA starts at B.

questions.q: How many lines can pass through a single point, and through two different points?
questions.a: Infinitely many through one point; exactly one through two points
questions.e: Two points fix exactly one line.

questions.q: How many degrees does the minute hand turn in {m} minutes?
questions.e: 60 minutes = 360°, so each minute = 6°: {m} × 6° = {ans}°.

questions.q: How many right angles make {d}°?
questions.e: {d}° ÷ 90° = {ans} right angles.

questions.q: Anil faces North and turns clockwise through three right angles. Which way does he face now?
Facing East, Riya turns anticlockwise through 270°. Which way does she face?
questions.e: Anticlockwise from East: N (90°), W (180°), S (270°).

questions.q: An angle measures {a}°. What is the measure of its reflex angle?
questions.e: Reflex angle = 360° − {a}° = {ans}°.

questions.q: An angle is double of {x}. What type of angle is it?
questions.e: Double the angle first, then classify: {ans}.

questions.q: An angle is double of {x}. What type of angle is it?
questions.e: Double the angle first, then classify: {ans}.

questions.q: At 4:00, what is the reflex angle between the hands of a clock?
questions.e: The smaller angle is 4 × 30° = 120°; reflex = 360° − 120° = 240°.

questions.q: At which whole-hour time do the clock hands make a straight angle?
questions.e: At 6:00 the hands point in opposite directions: 180°.

questions.q: A student measures an acute angle but reads {r}° from the wrong scale. What is the true measure?
questions.e: The two scales add to 180°: 180° − {r}° = {ans}°.

questions.q: How can you draw an angle of 250° with a 180° protractor?
questions.a: Draw 110° and mark the reflex angle outside it
w: Draw 250° directly on the outer scale
questions.e: 360° − 250° = 110°; the outside (reflex) angle of 110° is 250°.

questions.q: Two angles together make a straight angle. One is {a}°. What is the other?
questions.e: A straight angle is 180°: 180° − {a}° = {ans}°.

questions.q: Four angles meet at a point. Three of them are {a}°, {b}° and {c}°. Find the fourth.
questions.e: Angles around a point add to 360°: 360° − {a}° − {b}° − {c}° = {ans}°.
